text: `curl -i http://localhost:8080/` returns `502 Bad Gateway`. That's nginx failing to reach whatever it proxies to, not a problem with port 8080 itself (nginx answers -- it just can't get a response from upstream). Check the error log for the exact target it tried: `sudo tail /var/log/nginx/error.log`.

The log shows nginx trying to connect to `unix:/run/backend/app.sock`, and failing because that path doesn't exist. This proxy talks to its backend over a unix domain socket, not a TCP host:port -- so `ss -tlnp` won't show it. List what socket files actually exist instead: `ls -la /run/backend/`.
The backend's real socket is `/run/backend/app-v2.sock` -- a newer filename from a recent rollout. The proxy's config was never updated to match. Find it: `grep -rn proxy_pass /etc/nginx/`.
Fix `proxy_pass` in `/etc/nginx/conf.d/app.conf` to point at `http://unix:/run/backend/app-v2.sock;`, then `sudo nginx -t && sudo nginx -s reload`. Re-test `curl http://localhost:8080/`.
